Let the inner radius be \(r\) m.
Inner circumference \(= 2\pi r = 440\)
\(2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r = 440\)
\(r = \frac{440 \times 7}{44} = 70\) m
The track is 14 m wide, so outer radius \(= 70 + 14 = 84\) m.

So, the radius of the outer circle is 84 m.

Let the son's present age be \(x\) years. Then Shyam's present age is \(4x\) years.
Five years ago: son \(= x - 5\), Shyam \(= 4x - 5\).
\(4x - 5 = 9(x - 5)\)
\(4x - 5 = 9x - 45\)
\(5x = 40\), so \(x = 8\).
Shyam's age \(= 4 \times 8 = 32\) years.
Check: five years ago Shyam was 27 and his son 3, and \(27 = 9 \times 3\).

So, Shyam is 32 years old.

The hundreds digit can be any of the 3 digits, the tens digit any of the remaining 2, and the units digit the last one: \(3 \times 2 \times 1 = 6\) numbers.
Starting with 1: 156, 165
Starting with 5: 516, 561
Starting with 6: 615, 651

So, the numbers are 156, 165, 516, 561, 615 and 651.

The printed expression has a stray "?" after the small bracket; it is read as \(16-[5-2+\{7 \text{ of } 2-(6\div 3\times 2-1+3)\}]\).
Innermost bracket first (division, then multiplication, then subtraction and addition):
\(6 \div 3 \times 2 - 1 + 3 = 2 \times 2 - 1 + 3 = 4 - 1 + 3 = 6\)
Curly bracket: \(7 \text{ of } 2 - 6 = 14 - 6 = 8\)
Square bracket: \(5 - 2 + 8 = 11\)
Finally: \(16 - 11 = 5\)

So, the answer is 5.
answers.notice: A stray question mark is printed inside the curly bracket. Ignoring it, the expression simplifies to 5.

Ratio of ages \(= 2 : 4 : 8 = 1 : 2 : 4\)
Sum of the parts \(= 1 + 2 + 4 = 7\)
First boy (2 years): \(\frac{1}{7} \times 70 = \) Rs 10
Second boy (4 years): \(\frac{2}{7} \times 70 = \) Rs 20
Third boy (8 years): \(\frac{4}{7} \times 70 = \) Rs 40
Check: \(10 + 20 + 40 = 70\).

So, they get Rs 10, Rs 20 and Rs 40.

Fewer students make the ration last longer (inverse proportion).
Total ration \(= 180 \times 20 = 3600\) student-days.
Students for 25 days \(= \frac{3600}{25} = 144\)
Students who must leave \(= 180 - 144 = 36\)

So, 36 students should leave the camp.

Pass marks \(= 251 + 19 = 270\)
Let the maximum marks be \(M\).
45% of \(M = 270\)
\(M = \frac{270 \times 100}{45} = 600\)

So, the maximum marks are 600.

Selling price of 3 apples = Rs 10, so selling price of 300 apples \(= \frac{10}{3} \times 300 = \text{Rs } 1000\)
Gain = Rs 400, so cost price of 300 apples \(= 1000 - 400 = \text{Rs } 600\)
Cost price of one apple \(= \frac{600}{300} = \text{Rs } 2\) (that is, 3 apples for Rs 6)
Gain % \(= \frac{400}{600} \times 100 = \frac{200}{3} = 66\frac{2}{3}\%\)

So, he bought the apples at Rs 2 each (3 for Rs 6) and his gain was \(66\frac{2}{3}\%\).

The comma between the two powers is read as a multiplication sign.
\(\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{-5} \times \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{-11} = \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{8x}\)
Using \(a^m \times a^n = a^{m+n}\):
\(\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{-16} = \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{8x}\)
The bases are equal, so the powers are equal: \(8x = -16\)
\(x = -2\)

So, \(x = -2\).
answers.notice: The sign between the two powers is printed as a comma. The solution reads it as multiplication, which gives x = -2; read as division, x would be 3/4.

answers.solution:
Take his starting point as the origin, with east and north as the two directions.

North-west is exactly between north and west, so walking 13 m north-west moves him \(\frac{13}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 9.19\) m west and \(9.19\) m north.

Walking 5 m south then brings him back to \(9.19 - 5 = 4.19\) m north of the start, still \(9.19\) m west.

By Pythagoras, his distance from the start is \(\sqrt{9.19^2 + 4.19^2} = \sqrt{84.5 + 17.6} = \sqrt{102.1} \approx 10.1\) m.

So he is about 10.1 m from his initial position.
answers.notice: The answer usually given is 12 m, from the 5, 12, 13 right triangle, but that does not follow from the directions as printed. Walking 13 m north-west and then 5 m south leaves him about 10.1 m from where he started, which is the answer worked out here.

In the figure each side of the quadrilateral is extended once, and the four marked angles 90°, 50°, 110° and x are its exterior angles, one at each vertex.
The exterior angles of any polygon, taken one at each vertex, add up to 360°.
\(90^\circ + 50^\circ + 110^\circ + x = 360^\circ\)
\(250^\circ + x = 360^\circ\)
\(x = 110^\circ\)
Check with interior angles: \(90^\circ + 130^\circ + 70^\circ + 70^\circ = 360^\circ\). Correct.

So, \(x = 110^\circ\).

Distance on 1 litre \(= \frac{432}{48} = 9\) km
Distance on 20 litres \(= 9 \times 20 = 180\) km

So, the car would travel 180 km.

The semicircle APC stands on AC as diameter, so AC = 10 cm, and it reaches 5 cm in to P; the semicircle BPD reaches the other 5 cm. So ABDC is a square of side 10 cm, and P is its centre.
Let O be the midpoint of AC and M the midpoint of AB. The shaded region lies inside the square AMPO of side 5 cm and outside the arc AP, which is a quarter of the circle with centre O and radius 5 cm.
Area of square AMPO \(= 5 \times 5 = 25\) cm²
Area of quarter circle \(= \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 5 \times 5 = \frac{275}{14}\) cm²
Shaded area \(= 25 - \frac{275}{14} = \frac{350 - 275}{14} = \frac{75}{14}\) cm²

So, the area of the shaded region is \(\frac{75}{14} = 5\frac{5}{14}\) cm² (about 5.36 cm²).

Write the dividend in descending powers: \(-4x^2 + x + 6\).
Step 1: \(\frac{-4x^2}{x} = -4x\); \(-4x(x - 3) = -4x^2 + 12x\); subtract: \((-4x^2 + x) - (-4x^2 + 12x) = -11x\). Bring down 6: \(-11x + 6\).
Step 2: \(\frac{-11x}{x} = -11\); \(-11(x - 3) = -11x + 33\); subtract: \(6 - 33 = -27\).
Check: \((x - 3)(-4x - 11) - 27 = -4x^2 + x + 33 - 27 = -4x^2 + x + 6\). Correct.

So, the quotient is \(-4x - 11\) and the remainder is \(-27\).

x and y vary inversely, so \(xy\) is constant.
\(xy = 10 \times 6 = 60\)
When \(x = 15\): \(15 \times y = 60\), so \(y = 4\).

So, \(y = 4\).

Horse: SP = Rs 12000 at a loss of 20%.
CP of horse \(= \frac{12000 \times 100}{100 - 20} = \frac{12000 \times 100}{80} = \) Rs 15000
Cow: SP = Rs 12000 at a gain of 20%.
CP of cow \(= \frac{12000 \times 100}{100 + 20} = \frac{12000 \times 100}{120} = \) Rs 10000
Total CP \(= 15000 + 10000 = \) Rs 25000
Total SP \(= 12000 + 12000 = \) Rs 24000
SP is less than CP, so there is a loss of \(25000 - 24000 = \) Rs 1000.
Loss % \(= \frac{1000}{25000} \times 100 = 4\%\)

So, overall he has a loss of Rs 1000, that is 4%.

A's one day's work \(= \frac{1}{6}\); B's one day's work \(= \frac{1}{8}\).
Work done by A in 3 days \(= \frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2}\)
Work done by B in 3 days \(= \frac{3}{8}\)
Work done by C in 3 days \(= 1 - \frac{1}{2} - \frac{3}{8} = \frac{8 - 4 - 3}{8} = \frac{1}{8}\)
Shares are in the ratio of work done: \(\frac{1}{2} : \frac{3}{8} : \frac{1}{8} = 4 : 3 : 1\)
A's share \(= \frac{4}{8} \times 600 = \) Rs 300
B's share \(= \frac{3}{8} \times 600 = \) Rs 225
C's share \(= \frac{1}{8} \times 600 = \) Rs 75

So, A gets Rs 300, B gets Rs 225 and C gets Rs 75.
answers.finalAnswer: A Rs 300; B Rs 225; C Rs 75

Six years ago, let A's age be \(4k\) and B's age be \(3k\).
Present ages: A \(= 4k + 6\), B \(= 3k + 6\).
Nine years from now: A \(= 4k + 15\), B \(= 3k + 15\).
\(\frac{4k + 15}{3k + 15} = \frac{7}{6}\)
\(6(4k + 15) = 7(3k + 15)\)
\(24k + 90 = 21k + 105\)
\(3k = 15\), so \(k = 5\)
A's present age \(= 4 \times 5 + 6 = 26\) years
B's present age \(= 3 \times 5 + 6 = 21\) years
Check: six years ago 20 : 15 = 4 : 3; after nine years 35 : 30 = 7 : 6.

So, A is 26 years old and B is 21 years old.

(a) The sign between the two terms of the denominator is missing in print; it is read as \(\frac{5^{n+2} - 6 \times 5^{n+1}}{13 \times 5^{n} - 2 \times 5^{n+1}}\).
Numerator \(= 5^n \times 5^2 - 6 \times 5^n \times 5 = 5^n(25 - 30) = -5 \times 5^n\)
Denominator \(= 13 \times 5^n - 2 \times 5^n \times 5 = 5^n(13 - 10) = 3 \times 5^n\)
Value \(= \frac{-5 \times 5^n}{3 \times 5^n} = -\frac{5}{3}\)

(b) HCF by division:
\(1309 = 1 \times 1071 + 238\)
\(1071 = 4 \times 238 + 119\)
\(238 = 2 \times 119 + 0\)
So HCF = 119.
(Also \(1071 = 3^2 \times 7 \times 17\) and \(1309 = 7 \times 11 \times 17\), so HCF \(= 7 \times 17 = 119\).)
LCM \(= \frac{1071 \times 1309}{119} = 1071 \times 11 = 11781\)

So, (a) \(-\frac{5}{3}\); (b) HCF = 119 and LCM = 11781.
answers.notice: In part (a) the sign between the two terms of the denominator is not printed. The solution reads it as a minus, the usual form of this question, which gives -5/3; with a plus sign the value would be -5/23.

(a) The man and the train move in opposite directions, so the relative speed is \(49 + 5 = 54\) km/hr.
\(54 \text{ km/hr} = 54 \times \frac{5}{18} = 15\) m/s
The train passes the man in 12 seconds, so its length \(= 15 \times 12 = 180\) m.

(b) The two trains move in opposite directions, so the relative speed is \(49 + 41 = 90\) km/hr \(= 90 \times \frac{5}{18} = 25\) m/s.
Distance to cover = sum of the lengths \(= 180 + 160 = 340\) m
Time \(= \frac{340}{25} = 13.6\) seconds

So, (a) the train is 180 m long; (b) it takes 13.6 seconds to pass the other train.

Pipe fills in 1 hour \(= \frac{1}{6}\) of the tank.
With the leak, the tank fills in 1 hour \(= \frac{1}{7}\) of the tank.
Leak empties in 1 hour \(= \frac{1}{6} - \frac{1}{7} = \frac{7 - 6}{42} = \frac{1}{42}\) of the tank.
So the leak alone empties the full tank in 42 hours.

So, the leak will empty the full tank in 42 hours.

Time needed for 1 kg \(= 3 \text{ hours/day} \times 12 \text{ days} = 36\) hours
Time needed for 10 kg \(= 36 \times 10 = 360\) hours
Spinning 4 hours a day, number of days \(= \frac{360}{4} = 90\)

So, she will take 90 days.

Outer volume \(= 10 \times 8 \times 7 = 560\) cm³
The wood is 1 cm thick on every face, so each inner dimension is 2 cm less:
Inner dimensions \(= 8 \text{ cm} \times 6 \text{ cm} \times 5 \text{ cm}\)
Inner volume \(= 8 \times 6 \times 5 = 240\) cm³
Volume of wood \(= 560 - 240 = 320\) cm³
Cost \(= 320 \times 2 = \) Rs 640

So, the wood for the box costs Rs 640.

Total expenditure \(= 400 + 400 + 200 + 100 + 50 + 50 = 1200\)
Central angle of each item \(= \frac{\text{expenditure}}{1200} \times 360^\circ\)
Food: \(\frac{400}{1200} \times 360^\circ = 120^\circ\)
Rent: \(\frac{400}{1200} \times 360^\circ = 120^\circ\)
Clothing: \(\frac{200}{1200} \times 360^\circ = 60^\circ\)
Education: \(\frac{100}{1200} \times 360^\circ = 30^\circ\)
Litigation: \(\frac{50}{1200} \times 360^\circ = 15^\circ\)
Others: \(\frac{50}{1200} \times 360^\circ = 15^\circ\)
Check: \(120 + 120 + 60 + 30 + 15 + 15 = 360^\circ\).
To draw: draw a circle of any convenient radius and one radius from the centre. With a protractor, mark off sectors of 120°, 120°, 60°, 30°, 15° and 15° one after another, and label each sector with its item.

So, the pie chart has sectors Food 120°, Rent 120°, Clothing 60°, Education 30°, Litigation 15° and Others 15°.
answers.finalAnswer: Pie chart: Food 120°; Rent 120°; Clothing 60°; Education 30°; Litigation 15°; Others 15°

Let the interior angle be \(I\). Then the exterior angle is \(\frac{I}{3}\).
Interior angle + exterior angle \(= 180^\circ\)
\(I + \frac{I}{3} = 180^\circ\)
\(\frac{4I}{3} = 180^\circ\), so \(I = 135^\circ\)
Exterior angle \(= 180^\circ - 135^\circ = 45^\circ\)
Number of sides \(= \frac{360^\circ}{45^\circ} = 8\)

So, the polygon has 8 sides.
